conclusion: You are a non-secretor: neither of your versions of the FUT2 gene works, so your saliva and other body fluids do not carry the blood group sugars (the same sugar tags that decide your ABO blood group) that most people release into them. About 1 in 5 people of European ancestry are non-secretors. It is not a disease. It changes which germs can attach to the lining of the gut: non-secretors are largely protected from the most common kinds of norovirus, the winter vomiting bug, and may be more prone to certain other infections.

You are a weak secretor: your versions of the FUT2 gene work only partly, so your saliva and other body fluids carry less of the blood group sugars (the sugar tags that decide your ABO blood group) than usual. This reduced-activity version is common in East Asia and rare elsewhere. It is not a disease.

You are a secretor: at least one of your versions of the FUT2 gene works, so your saliva and other body fluids carry your blood group sugars, the same sugar tags that decide your ABO blood group. About 4 in 5 people are secretors, and one working copy is enough. It is not a disease, and it is the usual state.
